**Translation provenance check, 2026-09-12:** The evidence does **not** support attributing all incorrect translations to Transifex. The audit contains **4,061 changed values from the supplied uncommitted pull** and **16,020 additional findings in existing local values**. These are audit findings, including uncertain candidates, not counts of proven translation errors. The latter rows have no captured Transifex value or service-side provenance.

A concrete counterexample is [bdb3b1588](https://github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/bdb3b15886a749b725b5290ba0109fcba955f983), dated 2026-09-05, whose message describes finishing Bosnian by using Croatian as a base and translating remaining fields. Its diff replaces English placeholders in `bs.i18n.json` with the incorrect Serbian values `Double-Bounce = Исцртавај дворед са три тачкице` and `Node_memory_usage_rss = Node искоришћење меморије: постављена вредност`. Thus these errors entered Bosnian through the earlier local completion batch, before the pull audited here; there are **zero Bosnian rows in that captured pull**. This establishes the local introduction path, not the ultimate origin of every copied base-language string. The wrong Bosnian values were repaired in [48b6b1bb2](https://github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/48b6b1bb2a5d76ee7ae27d970ae103bf5cd0d95e).

Earlier “all translated” counts measured whether values differed from English; they did not establish correct language or meaning. The provenance of the other local findings remains individually unverified. No Transifex author/history API was queried, and no upload was performed. Preserve correct human translations and continue contextual repairs rather than treating every local finding as a bad Transifex translation.

The browser regressions are registered and syntax-checked; live Meteor execution remains unavailable. The correction list now contains **2,392 values**.

**Romanian correction batch, 2026-09-12:** [9c974f034](https://github.com/wekan/wekan/commit/9c974f0340aa70c173e90aef466742234c6f493a) corrects **160 values** across `ro.i18n.json` and `ro-RO.i18n.json`: account protection, activity messages, archive actions, board settings and basic kanban labels. Native wording, source tokens and actual sprintf argument order pass regression checks, including removal of the spurious digit in subtask notifications. The first batch addresses **499 audited values in 101 language files** (497 values required changes; two already matched the reviewed correction):

- 45 JSON examples now use valid JSON and literal `title` and `description` property names, preserving translated sample prose where recoverable.
- 128 Chinese-language strings use kanban terminology `看板` instead of the corporate board-of-directors term `董事会`.
- Mixed-script fragments were corrected in Assamese, Dzongkha, Khmer and Macedonian; the empty Russian rule phrase was supplied.
- Foreign or untranslated calendar labels were replaced with target-language terminology from [Unicode CLDR 48.2](https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr-json). Its license is retained in [Unicode-LICENSE.txt](Unicode-LICENSE.txt).
- A reviewed correction list and repeatable local repair command preserve newer translations: `node releases/translations/repair-audited-translations.mjs --apply`.

Correction regression checks pass for values, placeholders, JSON examples, key order, idempotency and preservation of newer wording. Human-preference checks and calendar-display checks also pass. The browser regression is syntax-checked; a live Meteor UI was unavailable. The repository-wide completeness check still reports existing English-valued candidates in six locales; the full audit is **not yet completely resolved**. ## Recommendation

Review per key. Restore confirmed wrong-language, broken-example and
contaminated values from the previous correct target-language text. Preserve
verified correct-language improvements. Review uncertain words in context;
do not blanket-revert a locale or accept every non-English replacement.

Local values are comparison evidence, not a guarantee that every prior
translation was correct. The detailed original inventory is retained locally
in `.tools/tmp/transifex-uncommitted-audit.json`. This documentation now includes
all its changed keys and complete before/after values, so that temporary file
is not required to read or review the tables.

## Audit of every current local language file

All 246 files and 662,970 values were screened on 2026-09-12. Each file contains the 2,695 English source keys; JSON parsing found no duplicate keys or invalid files. Screening checks placeholders, empty values, JSON examples, response preambles, script mixtures, English remnants and repeated foreign-language seeds. Existing invariant-aware translation scanners were reused.

The tables below add 16,020 flagged keys beyond the original pull inventory. Keys already in the pull tables are not repeated. Here **Translation local value means the current working-file value**. No Transifex value is available for these additional keys: the remote service was not queried, and committed local values are not treated as Transifex evidence.

This is an all-values screening audit with inspected examples, not a native-speaker certification of every unflagged phrase. Review categories include legitimate loanwords, romanization and shared terminology. Exact cross-language equality alone is insufficient to prove an error. Related-language candidates require vocabulary review; calendar names may be accepted technical terms. No locale files were changed.
